headline: Nasdaq-100 futures remain halted about an hour before the scheduled Sunday CME restart; tail low, stress high on unresolved Hormuz disruption and a steepening long end
body:
No live Nasdaq-100 price path exists at this timestamp. CME equity index futures remain inside the weekend halt and are scheduled to restart near 22:00 UTC, roughly an hour after this assessment, so the evaluation rests on the last completed cash session, verified cross-asset levels and the current macro and geopolitical backdrop rather than on observed intraday structure.

The cash Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 30,046.14, down 0.13% inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below its 30,762.20 52-week high, after a second consecutive winning week for the major U.S. indices. VIX finished at 14.25, down 2.60%, which keeps implied volatility subdued against the high stress reading. Treasury constant-maturity yields stood at 4.15% for the 2Y, 4.32% for the 5Y, 4.63% for the 10Y and 5.21% for the 30Y at the latest H.15 publication, with last week's 30-year auction clearing at 5.216%, the highest since 2007, and a 20-year sale due Wednesday into a steepening curve.

Friday's internals were split rather than one-way. Broadcom fell 5.94% on a mix of AI-financing concerns and an actively exploited VMware vCenter vulnerability, and Applied Materials dropped despite beating on revenue, while AMD rose 6.5% and Micron added 2.3%. Sector context from the shared delayed cross-asset feed shows technology down 0.46% and software groups down more than 1% on the latest session, with megacap direction mixed. That dispersion argues for uncertainty rather than persistent directional efficiency.

The energy and geopolitical backdrop remains the dominant stress channel. WTI trades at $82.40, up 1.42% on the day and roughly 5% on the week, with Brent at $88.52, as Strait of Hormuz traffic stays depressed and global stockpiles draw down. A UAE-affiliated ADNOC tanker was attacked in the strait on Friday, while Iran's foreign minister continues talks with Oman on shipping routes, leaving the headline set genuinely two-sided rather than one-directional.

Tail therefore stays in the low band. The observed evidence contains no persistent no-retracement structure, no failed-retracement extension and no index holding near an extreme, and none of that can be observed at all while the market is halted. Stress remains high because an unresolved supply disruption, elevated crude and rising global long yields can still produce a large but recoverable drawdown. A narrow observation window is flagged around the scheduled Sunday restart, where thin liquidity and weekend headline risk concentrate.

The week ahead adds known checkpoints rather than observed risk: Empire State and NAHB on Monday, housing and industrial production on Tuesday, the 20-year auction and July FOMC minutes on Wednesday, jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed survey and Walmart on Thursday, and flash PMIs on Friday. These are scheduled catalysts, and under the fixed mapping they inform stress and confidence until an actual price path is available to score.

A secondary rise to 16-17 is carried across the Monday U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC and the first hour after it, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the first genuine tail evidence of the new week.
